title: Add integration tests for multi-tenant burst scenarios (fairness, cooldowns, denial codes)
author: Benji Okafor
description: This PR adds a new set of multi-tenant integration tests for Dedicated Burst admission that exercise: (1) fairness enforcement across tenants under sustained contention, (2) cooldown window behavior after a tenant hits its configured burst cap, and (3) correctness/stability of denial reason codes returned to routing/gateway. Motivation: our existing unit tests cover token-bucket math and individual policy rules, but we were missing end-to-end coverage for the emergent behavior when multiple tenants are simultaneously bursting and the admission controller is combining policy + telemetry + fairness state. These tests are designed to be deterministic (fake clock + fixed seeds) and to fail with actionable diffs (snapshot of per-tenant admit/deny timelines + reason distributions). Scenarios included: (a) 3 equal-priority tenants contend for a shared pool: verify admitted share stays within tolerance and no tenant is starved; (b) mixed priority tiers (gold/silver) with anti-starvation floor: verify higher tier gets preference without driving lower tier to zero admits; (c) tenant cap reached then cooldown: verify immediate denials return TENANT_CAP_REACHED, subsequent requests during cooldown return COOLDOWN_ACTIVE, and requests after cooldown recover; (d) pool saturation with fleet safety guardrail: verify BURST_POOL_SATURATED vs FLEET_SAFETY_TRIPPED are mutually exclusive and stable under retries; (e) policy disabled / tenant not enabled: verify POLICY_DISABLED and that fairness state is not mutated for non-burst tenants. Notes: these tests depend on the denial code contract introduced in pr-23795 and the fairness state machine from pr-23777; they also align with determinism expectations from the admission semantics ADR (routing must not observe oscillating denial codes under identical inputs).
commits: itest/burst: add multi-tenant harness with fake clock + deterministic scheduler
itest/burst: add fairness contention scenarios (equal priority + mixed tier)
itest/burst: add cooldown and cap transition assertions w/ reason code snapshots
admission: export redacted debug snapshot for tests only (build tag itest)
ci: wire burst integration tests into presubmit with bounded runtime
testing: go test ./services/burst-admission/itest -run TestMultiTenant -count=1; go test ./services/burst-admission/itest -run TestMixedTiers_NoStarvation -count=20 (flake check); presubmit: burst-admission-itest (added in this PR).
reviewer_comments: Jordan Lee: The fairness assertions look good, but can we avoid hardcoding exact admit counts? I’d prefer tolerances + clear failure output so we don’t break on minor scheduling changes.

Benji Okafor (author): Updated to assert ratios within +/-7% over a 2m simulated window and added a failure dump of (tenant -> admitted, denied_by_reason) + timeline sample. Also seeded the scheduler and removed a couple of time-based sleeps in favor of FakeClock.Advance().

Keiko Yamamoto: Cooldown scenario: please validate the transition between TENANT_CAP_REACHED and COOLDOWN_ACTIVE explicitly. We’ve had bugs where we returned CAP_REACHED throughout cooldown and it confused CS.

Benji Okafor (author): Added assertions for the exact sequence: first denial after crossing cap -> TENANT_CAP_REACHED; next N requests within cooldown -> COOLDOWN_ACTIVE; first request after cooldown expiry -> admitted (or if pool saturated, saturated reason only).
Mina Haddad: For routing determinism, do we test that retries with same request_id don’t flip denial reasons? That’s been a customer-visible pain point.

Benji Okafor (author): Added TestDenialReasons_StableUnderRetry with idempotency key held constant. It asserts reason codes and retry-after hints are stable unless telemetry epoch advances (we simulate that explicitly).
Sean Gallagher: Please keep runtime bounded. This will be on presubmit. Can we cap the number of iterations and still catch regressions?
Benji Okafor (author): Reduced iterations, switched to simulated time, and added -short behavior (skips the 20x flake loop). Presubmit runs the short suite; nightly runs the full suite.
release_notes: Internal: Added deterministic multi-tenant integration coverage for burst admission fairness/cooldowns/denial code contracts; wired into presubmit as a bounded integration check.
notes: The itest-only debug snapshot is guarded behind an itest build tag and returns redacted state (no tenant names; only opaque tenant IDs + counters). If this becomes a maintenance burden, we can migrate the snapshot to the existing internal debug endpoint introduced in the support tooling work (ENG-4881) and have tests call it via localhost.
